name: FhirHubPrescription
title: fhir-hub prescription
description: One prescription written in the session.

element.short: Present only when the product falls under the Opiumwet
One G-Standaard coding, at the level Prescriptor prescribed at, plus an ATC when it supplies one
element.comment: Exactly one G-Standaard coding is emitted — PRK, HPK or GPK, whichever level the prescription was written at — so match on whichever is present rather than looking for PRK. This is the reverse of the input side, where a PRK or HPK the host sends is expanded to a PRK + GPK (+ HPK) set for medication surveillance. CodeableConcept.text carries the product description.

element.short: Always a data-absent-reason of 'unknown', never a reference
element.comment: MedicationRequest.subject is 1..1 in base R4, but a session result carries no patient identity: fhir-hub is stateless and never stored the Patient the host pushed in. data-absent-reason is the FHIR idiom for a mandatory element that genuinely cannot be supplied, and is honest about the gap in a way an invented reference would not be. Do not resolve it; correlate on the session id you polled with.

constraint.human: subject carries a data-absent-reason rather than a reference: a session result has no patient identity to point at.

element.comment: This is the authoritative form of the dosing instruction. Dosage.text accompanies it for readers that cannot interpret Tabel 25, and no timing or doseAndRate is derived from it.
The G-Standaard thesaurus basiseenheden, not UCUM: 'ST' (stuks) has no UCUM equivalent.
